summary: [Phase 1] Organizer NPS survey triggered at post-onboarding milestone

ai.s: Sends new organisers an NPS email a set number of days after onboarding completes, capturing early satisfaction before their first event.
ai.pr: There was no early signal on organiser satisfaction with the setup experience, when there is still time to course-correct.
ai.wy: Retention: an early-warning signal for Customer Success, secondary to the post-event organiser NPS.
ai.oc: Specified: a 0-10 NPS email after a configurable delay (default 7 days), tagged 'post-onboarding', within the shared 30-day cap, with CS alerts on detractors.

summary: [Phase 1] No-login feedback landing page for survey responses

ai.s: Provides a fast, mobile-friendly, no-login landing page where survey recipients complete their feedback in under 60 seconds.
ai.pr: Response rates drop sharply when users must log in or face a complex form, so every survey link needs a frictionless page.
ai.wy: Maximise response rates for the NPS/CSAT feedback programme.
ai.oc: Specified: tokenised no-login page loading under 2 seconds on 4G, at most 3-4 questions, thank-you and already-responded messages, and per-event branding.

summary: [Phase 1] Email survey trigger timing and opt-out configuration

ai.s: Adds admin controls for feedback email timing and lets organisers opt individual events out of visitor and exhibitor surveys.
ai.pr: Without configurable triggers and opt-outs, surveys could go out at the wrong time or to audiences organisers had not agreed to survey.
ai.wy: Respect client preferences, e.g. private or NDA-governed events, while keeping the process under control.
ai.oc: Specified: global and per-event send delay, a global on/off, event-level opt-out that never suppresses organiser NPS, optional reminders and bounce logs.

summary: [Phase 1] Feedback data export and access for analysis

ai.s: Makes all collected survey responses exportable in a structured format so Product and CS can analyse them in existing BI tools.
ai.pr: Feedback data needed to be usable straight after Phase 1 launch without building a reporting interface.
ai.wy: Data accessibility and portability for the NPS/Feedback Collection programme.
ai.oc: Specified: on-demand CSV export with respondent type, event, survey type, score, text, timestamp and channel, confirmed portability and a documented retention policy.

summary: [Phase 2] In-platform CSAT widget triggered by key user actions

ai.s: Shows a small, dismissible in-platform CSAT prompt after users complete key actions such as capturing a lead or booking a meeting.
ai.pr: Email surveys are retrospective and do not show which specific features cause friction in the moment.
ai.wy: More accurate, actionable, feature-level satisfaction data for the product team.
ai.oc: Specified: admin-configurable trigger rules, a non-blocking 1-5 or thumbs widget, a 14-day per-user cap and responses tagged by action, module and persona.

summary: [Phase 2] Module-specific thumbs up/down feedback on platform features

ai.s: Adds one-tap thumbs up/down feedback on individual platform modules to show which features work and which cause friction.
ai.pr: NPS and CSAT give aggregate scores but do not pinpoint which modules are causing friction.
ai.wy: High-volume micro-feedback builds a module-level signal over time.
ai.oc: Specified: contextual thumbs prompts on admin-configured modules, an optional comment, once per module per event, with aggregate counts in the data export.

summary: [Phase 2] Mobile in-app CSAT prompts post-event

ai.s: Prompts visitors and exhibitors in the mobile app for a CSAT rating when the event closes, deduplicated against email responses.
ai.pr: Post-event email surveys compete with inbox noise and are often opened late, even though many users experience the event mainly through the app.
ai.wy: Capture feedback while recall is highest, with higher completion than email.
ai.oc: Specified: an in-app modal on event close for active app users, completable in 30 seconds, one reminder, email link invalidated after an in-app response.

summary: Native Template Library

ai.s: Adds a native template gallery to the App Builder so any TAM can preview and apply a pre-built mobile homepage template in one click.
ai.pr: TAMs had no native templates; one TAM kept HTML/CSS templates in a dummy event, and others had to copy raw code between Admin Panel environments.
ai.wy: Cut manual TAM setup effort and remove dependency on one person's workaround.
ai.oc: Specified: a 'Choose Template' gallery with thumbnails and full previews, inserting editable HTML/CSS into the custom block, with an overwrite warning.

summary: Brand Asset Forms with Variable Substitution

ai.s: Adds brand asset forms to App Builder templates so TAMs enter colours, logo, background and font and the system generates the homepage HTML/CSS.
ai.pr: Even with templates, TAMs had to edit raw HTML/CSS to add client brand assets, which was error-prone and risked breaking live homepages.
ai.wy: Reduce TAM effort and errors in mobile app homepage setup.
ai.oc: Specified: templates with named variables, a validated form with colour picker and uploads, variable substitution with defaults, and re-editable asset values.

summary: Section Builder with Property Controls

ai.s: Adds a section builder to the App Builder homepage so TAMs can toggle, reorder and configure sections without editing code.
ai.pr: Layout changes beyond brand assets needed manual HTML/CSS edits or escalation to the design team.
ai.wy: Let TAMs meet varied client layout needs without design-team escalation.
ai.oc: Specified: templates as ordered sections with visibility toggles, drag-and-drop order and per-section properties, assembled into HTML/CSS with brand assets kept.

summary: Analytics strategy: map top user journeys & define event schema

ai.s: Defines the Admin Panel analytics strategy: the top user journeys to track and a signed-off event naming schema.
ai.pr: No agreed set of journeys or event naming existed, and poor schema design is hard to fix once historical data is collected.
ai.wy: A prerequisite source of truth for all in-app analytics instrumentation.
ai.oc: Specified: 5-10 mapped journeys, an object_action naming convention, standard event properties and a governance process, in a signed-off document.

summary: Integrate PostHog JS SDK into Admin Panel frontend

ai.s: Integrates the PostHog SDK into the Admin Panel frontend with route-change page views, consent gating and the EU cloud endpoint.
ai.pr: The Admin Panel captured no product analytics, and as an SPA its page views would not be tracked automatically.
ai.wy: Enables product analytics on Admin Panel usage, under the In-app analytics epic.
ai.oc: Specified: posthog-js on the EU host, API key from environment, virtual page views on route change, consent-only initialisation and disabled in local dev.

summary: Implement pseudonymous user identification on Admin Panel login

ai.s: Identifies logged-in Admin Panel users in PostHog by internal ID only, so per-user behaviour can be analysed without sending PII.
ai.pr: PostHog tracks anonymous users by default, and GDPR data minimisation rules out using emails or names as identifiers.
ai.wy: Per-user analytics while staying GDPR-compliant.
ai.oc: Specified: posthog.identify with the internal ID on login, non-PII properties only, reset on logout and legal/privacy sign-off.

summary: Instrument top Admin Panel user journeys with PostHog capture events

ai.s: Instruments the top Admin Panel journeys, such as event creation and exhibitor management, with structured PostHog events.
ai.pr: There was no structured data on how organisers navigate and use the Admin Panel.
ai.wy: Understand organiser behaviour to inform product decisions.
ai.oc: Specified: posthog.capture calls following the signed-off schema with standard properties and no PII, for event creation, registration, exhibitors, badges and agenda.

summary: Build funnel and retention reports in PostHog for top user journeys

ai.s: Builds PostHog funnel and retention reports for top Admin Panel journeys to show where organisers drop off and how often they return.
ai.pr: Once events flow, the Product team still lacks actionable views of drop-off points and retention.
ai.wy: Surface friction points and engagement trends for the product backlog.
ai.oc: Specified: at least 2 funnels, 1 week-over-week retention cohort and a user path analysis in a shared project, with drop-offs logged for the backlog.

summary: Enable PostHog session replay with PII field masking in Admin Panel

ai.s: Enables PostHog session replay in the Admin Panel with all personal and sensitive fields masked.
ai.pr: The Product team could not watch real sessions to understand qualitative behaviour, and unmasked recordings of Admin Panel data would breach GDPR.
ai.wy: Qualitative usage insight without recording PII.
ai.oc: Specified: session recording enabled after a PII field audit, masking applied and tested in staging, a documented field list and legal sign-off before production.

summary: Create internal Product team analytics dashboard in PostHog

ai.s: Creates a shared PostHog dashboard of Admin Panel KPIs as the Product team's single source of truth for platform usage.
ai.pr: Without a shared dashboard, team members would build ad-hoc queries with inconsistent metric definitions.
ai.wy: Consistent usage metrics for product decisions and a regular review cadence.
ai.oc: Specified: 'Admin Panel — Product Analytics' with WAU, event creation funnel, top features, retention and replay links, plus a documented 800K events/month review threshold.

summary: Enforce session-registration form before Add-to-Schedule (Mobile)

ai.s: Makes the mobile app show a session's registration form before adding it to the schedule, matching the website, so answers are captured.
ai.pr: On mobile, Add to Schedule added sessions requiring registration immediately, so attendees' registration answers were never captured.
ai.wy: Parity with the website and complete registration data for organisers.
ai.oc: Specified: form shown on iPhone and Android for free sessions requiring registration, added only on valid submit, with clear full-session and session-limit messages.

summary: Migrate image resize Lambda and API Gateway from us-east-1 to eu-west-1 for production

ai.s: Moves the production image resize Lambda and API Gateway from us-east-1 to eu-west-1 alongside the rest of production.
ai.pr: The resize Lambda ran in us-east-1 while S3 and other production services ran in eu-west-1, adding latency, cross-region transfer costs and inconsistency.
ai.wy: Cut latency and data transfer costs and keep infrastructure in one region.
ai.oc: Specified: Lambda and API Gateway deployed in eu-west-1, S3 redirects and CloudFront updated, IAM checked, end-to-end tested and the old stack decommissioned.

summary: API endpoint for Client Manager (super admin) account management

ai.s: Provides API endpoints to create Client Manager super admin accounts, reset passwords and regenerate 2FA QR codes for automated staff onboarding.
ai.pr: Client Manager accounts for new TAM and Engineering joiners were created manually because no API existed.
ai.wy: Internal efficiency: the HR onboarding automation tool needs it to set up backend access automatically.
ai.oc: Requested: create-account, reset-password and Google Authenticator QR endpoints with documented authentication.

summary: Deploy clickhouse migrations

epic.summary: Download leads and Scanned me lists refactor

ai.s: Deploys ClickHouse migrations for the leads download and Scanned Me lists refactor (ticket has no further detail).
ai.pr: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; the description only links a related ticket.
ai.wy: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; part of the Download leads and Scanned me lists refactor.
ai.oc: Not clearly specified beyond the ticket title; the ticket is on hold.

summary: AutoUpdate system improvements

ai.s: Improves the AutoUpdates integration system with CSV export of sync history, clearer status icons, a smaller Genesis batch size and better error visibility.
ai.pr: Sync results lacked export and clear status icons, the Genesis batch size caused worker failures, and some errors and failed integrations were not visible on dashboards.
ai.wy: Internal request to make integration syncs more reliable and easier to monitor.
ai.oc: Specified: CSV export, status icons per outcome, Genesis batch cut from 15 to 5, 'lost during processing' errors emitted, and failed integrations visible.
